SAME-R / Detector transfer study

Does the smoke response transfer?

A spacecraft designer has tested an optical detector on four smoke materials. How closely can those tests predict its recorded response to a fifth? Try the comparison on fourteen NASA flight runs, then inspect the material the model gets wrong.

Withhold a whole material

1.25 V mean absolute error across 14 held-out runs

The model used one setting known before heating, the hot-to-cold heater resistance ratio (Rt/R0). Predicting every run from the median of the other materials gave 4.62 V mean absolute error. Using their mean gave 3.25 V. Even with its lower average error, the heater model put three of four Kapton runs on the wrong side of the 2 V comparison line.

Inspect a held-out material

Check against the published experiment

Meyer and colleagues report that two-thirds of their Teflon samples fell below the ISS detector alarm boundary. Figure 9b places that boundary at 2 V. In this narrower series, ISS scatter dropped by 1.005 V (run 79), 2.180 V (81) and 1.763 V (83). Two of three fell below 2 V. Using the absolute raw peak voltages puts the same two below the line.

The two fractions agree numerically. The paper combines more conditions and does not identify its plotted points by run number. Figure 9b labels the vertical axis as ISS detector signal. Applying its 2 V line to our baseline-corrected drop is exploratory. Reconstructing actual alarm decisions would require the published signal conversion, calibration and alarm logic. The Shuttle uses different hardware. Meyer et al., Figure 9 and §3.2 ↗

What to measure next

Repeat the comparison on withheld Kapton and Teflon specimens with a calibrated particle-size reference and the detector’s alarm-state channel. Include an unsaturated response for the large-particle smokes. Investigators selected heater targets for each material to produce measurable smoke. The ratio therefore carries information about the material and its test protocol. Applying this model to an unfamiliar material would need an independently chosen setting and new measurements. Meyer et al., experimental method ↗

Selection, calculation and uncertainty

NASA runs 73–86 form a consecutive convenience sample from 26–30 August 2010. We used the base run IDs at 8.1 cm/s inlet speed, 60 s nominal heating, 11 s primary aging and 8 s primary mixing. Later aged samples with suffixed IDs are excluded. Each physical test contributes once. Runs 75 and 85 repeated a protocol on different days aboard the ISS. They can appear on opposite sides of a run holdout and stay together in the material holdout. The five materials contribute between one and four runs apiece. These internal holdouts have no external validation cohort.

Each target is the preheat median voltage minus the minimum ISS scatter voltage in the first 300 s after recorded heater onset. The preheat window spans the preceding 30 s. We match TestNumber to the base test, check the self-test bit, retain recorded rows including duplicate whole-second timestamps, and report the peak cell. This is a five-minute signal feature. Several peaks cluster near the upper recorded response. Differences near saturation cannot establish the relative smoke concentration.

For every fold, fit an ordinary least-squares line from the training heater ratios to the training peak drops. Clip negative predicted drops to zero. Both baselines use only the training peaks. The material holdout excludes all runs of that material. The run holdout excludes one physical test. Error ranges describe the observed held-out runs. One silicone run cannot estimate repeat variability or establish a population detection rate.

Reproduce these results

Recompute the folds or verify original cells

Save the JSON and Python files together. Recompute every held-out prediction locally with Python 3.10 or later.

python detector-study.py --verify detector-study.json

To verify each workbook SHA-256, native cell, condition row and derived peak against NASA, install xlrd 2.0.2 and run the following command. The first run downloads the source table and fourteen workbooks into the specified directory.

python detector-study.py --verify detector-study.json --cache ./workbooks --download
